title: The grammar of reduction
mathematical_role: Show the direction and membership-preserving contract of a polynomial-time many-one reduction from A to B.
learning_objective: Read A <=_p B in the correct direction and understand that an efficient solver for B can be used after f to solve A.
literal_semantics: A and B denote decision problems/languages.
The directed arrow denotes the reduction map f from instances of A to instances of B.
The displayed relation x in A iff f(x) in B is the membership-preservation contract.
nonliteral_semantics: Circle size and spacing carry no complexity measure.
The drawing does not encode the running-time polynomial or a concrete reduction algorithm.

notes: This plate is retained as the primary positive control demonstrating that representation-first governance does not reject SVG when the object is intrinsically diagrammatic.

reproducibility_notes: The committed SVG is itself the complete vector source and is bound by exact Git blob identity.

derivatives.role: canonical current web plate and vector source

accessibility.alt_text: Directed gateways map one decision problem into another while preserving yes and no instances.
accessibility.long_description: A directed diagram maps problem A to problem B by f and states x in A if and only if f(x) is in B. The direction matters: a solver for B combined with the reduction yields a solver for A. The geometry of the circles is purely presentational.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Exact diagrammatic statement of the membership-preserving direction of a polynomial-time many-one reduction as already stated in the documentary text.
not_claimed: A concrete reduction between named NP-complete problems
